title: Renaming a node in a parent scene which has a child node in a child scene creates new nodes in the child scene instead of renaming the original node and preserving the relationships.
body:
### Tested versions

4.4.1

### System information

Windows 11 - intel i5 13600kf - rtx 4070

### Issue description

As you can see in the image below after I renamed StateMachine to LocomotionStateMachine in my Actor.tscn the Player scene which inherits from Actor.tscn now has the renamed nodes as well as two extra nodes called `LocomotionStateMachine#Idle` and `LocomotionStateMachine#Move`.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd15a5de-e8c4-4085-a51e-5aa247e86abe)

What I'd expect is the renamed node to keep the children and no extra new nodes to be created.
(The behaviour above with the extra nodes I'd assume should be happening if for example the old node got deleted instead of just renaming.)

### Steps to reproduce

EDIT:
1. In the MRP open all three scenes.
2. Check how they look.
3. Then go to the parent.tscn.
4. Rename ParentNode to ParentNodeTest (it doesn't matter what the name actually is).
5. Save the parent.tscn.
6. Switch tab to the child.tscn.
7. Observe how it looks now. It's a mess. Somehow renaming doesn't use the uid of the scene or what is going on?

Before renaming:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9dcbf28-5f52-496a-a006-28f8f8c4b0f8)

After renaming:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bc16361e-9c56-4321-b7e4-4b000dc6dcb4)

(8. Occasionally if you have a script with exported field pointing to one of the child nodes it can also break, not always for some reason though so I did not include it in the mrp).

----

Manual set up if you prefer doing it on your own:

Scenes are set like this:
Scene A (parent).
Scene B (inherits A)
(Essentially B extends A)

Scene A has a node called ABC.
Scene B inherits the ABC node.
Scene B added another node as a child of ABC called 123.
Save everything, keep the scenes open.
Go to the scene A and rename ABC to XYZ, and save.
Go to the scene B and observe you now have:
XYZ#123 and XYZ nodes instead of XYZ  with a child node 123.

----

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[InheritanceChangesMrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19614901/InheritanceChangesMrp.zip)
